**Abstract**

Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of topic categorization of documents after speech recognition of calls. This categorization consists of two important parts. The first one is text preprocessing for numerical data extraction and the second one is classification with machine learning algorithms. The main goal of this paper is to present how different text categorization methods were applied in order to improve a natural language call routing system. In this work we have experimented with different techniques from both parts of this categorization. From text preprocessing part, we tested a number of methods for the numerical data extraction including regular expressions, NER and rule-based approaches. From the machine learning part, we experimented with a number of well-known classification techniques like SVM, k-NN, random forests, decision trees. We tested our models on a dataset that we built. Our results show that we get good results when we combine the best numerical data extraction method (rule based approach) with a strong classifier (random forests or decision trees).

Our study has shown that this method can improve the performance of text classification and clustering tasks when transferring knowledge from one corpus (the source domain) to another corpus (the target domain). The proposed method selects features that are discriminative to the target domain and then uses a classifier that is trained on the source domain, but adapted to the target domain. By applying our method to several public datasets, we show that our approach yields better results than some common existing methods. Therefore, we recommend the use of adaptive ensembling as a tool for performing political document analysis.

Practical implications – In the process of facility management (FM), managers should pay attention to the selection of procurement route. By selecting appropriate procurement route, we can get the good ongoing buyer-supplier relationship.

Abstract

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization. The aim of this work was to identify the chemical compounds produced by *C. nivalis* that may be responsible for the pink color of snow algae. By using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and retention time alignment, we were able to identify three esterified derivatives of the carotenoid astaxanthin, all of which are new to science. These are astaxanthin diglucoside mono-ester (1), astaxanthin diglucoside di-ester (2), and astaxanthin diglucoside tri-ester (3). We found that esterification can occur between the hydroxyl groups of both ends of the carotenois aglycon or between one of the hydroxyl groups of both ends with the free hydroxyl group of a glucoside. The results indicate that the three identified ester derivatives have a similar retention time, and it was not possible to separate them by liquid chromatography. Therefore, only the molecular formulas were determined by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization, and the structures of the compounds were confirmed using tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS). The proposed chemical structures of astaxanthin diglucoside mono-ester and astaxanthin diglucoside di-ester were further verified by synthesis. The results provide new information about the secondary metabolites produced by *C. nivalis*.

Background: Leprosy is a chronic infectious disease caused by infection with Mycobacterium leprae. Drug resistance can occur when M. leprae undergoes changes that reduce the effectiveness of previously effective drug treatments. The aim of this research was to determine if drug resistant M. leprae can be isolated from patients with lepromatous leprosy that have not received antileprosy drug treatment.
Methods: Skin biopsies were obtained from three patients with lepromatous leprosy who had never been treated for their leprosy. The homogenates from these biopsies were tested using the mouse footpad method for drug sensitivity. The homogenates were tested against a single drug and multiple drugs at a range of concentrations to determine if the organisms that were isolated in these samples had any drug resistance.
Results: This research shows that all three of the patient samples contain M. leprae that are resistant to at least one anti-leprosy drug and that two of the patient samples also contain M. leprae which are resistant to multiple anti-leprosy drugs.
Conclusion: This work indicates that drug resistance occurs to some degree even before any anti-leprosy drugs have been given to treat a patient with lepromatous leprosy. These results suggest that leprosy screening programs should include drug sensitivity testing so that effective anti-leprosy drugs can be given to the patient to ensure that they will respond to the drug.

**Abstract**

Serotonin or melatonin was infused into the third cerebral ventricle (3rd V) or into the medial basal hypothalamus (MBH) of both intact ewes and ewes with lesions of the anterior hypothalamic area (AHA). These manipulations were performed to examine their effect on the release of luteinizing hormone (LH) in ovariectomized ewes that received estradiol benzoate and were super-ovulated, and also to observe the effects on ovulation. To determine the site(s) of action of these indoleamines, we tested whether pretreatment with p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA), which blocks synthesis of serotonin and melatonin, could reduce the response to infusions.

Results show that serotonergic fibers project to both the 3rd V and MBH in sheep. PCPA treatment inhibited the effect of 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT; serotonin) infusion on super-ovulated ewes. However, 5-HT was also effective when infused into the 3rd V of ewes that had lesions in AHA. Results also demonstrate that melatonin has no effect on LH release, but it does suppress ovulation. Additionally, PCPA did not block the effects of melatonin.

The data presented in this research suggest that: 

1. The site(s) of action of indoleamines on the super-ovulated estradiol benzoate-treated ewe are probably in the 3rd V or MBH. 
2. The site(s) of action are not in the AHA.
3. The 3rd V is not a site of action for the indoleamines.

Keywords: LH (luteinizing hormone), ovulation, sheep, indoleamines, serotonin, melatonin, hypothalamus, ventricle, p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA)

generations.raw_text: Submicron magnetic composite microspheres have been prepared by a new surfactant free controlled radical polymerization. Then, these particles were introduced into the monomer solution to synthesize the magnetic microspheres by controlled radical polymerization. In this paper, we also analyzed the structure, composition, morphology, and magnetic properties of the microspheres. Finally, we evaluated their biocompatibility using mouse embryonic fibroblast cells. We found that the synthesized microspheres did not show any significant toxicity at a concentration of up to 6 mg/mL. Therefore, our results proved that these magnetic composite microspheres have very nice application potential for biomedical field.

Abstract:
Leibowitz and his colleagues found that accommodation rests at an intermediate distance that shows wide inter-individual variation. They proposed that this intermediate dark focus is useful for correcting anomalous refractive errors, but this proposal was later questioned when different measurement techniques yielded discrepant results. We present data to support Leibowitz et al.'s model, using a mathematical method to estimate the optimal value of dark focus of accommodation in order to maximize the amount of positive diopter error corrected. This approach was validated against empirical values of accommodation and results from previously published clinical studies. Our findings show that Leibowitz et al.'s model can be applied in practice as a method of predicting the amount of positive diopter error that can be corrected. The abstract concludes by suggesting that these findings could be used to improve current theories about dark focus of accommodation and its use to correct refractive errors.
